papers.title: Disproportionate Effect of Sub-Micron Topography on Osteoconductive Capability of Titanium.
papers.abstract: Titanium micro-scale topography offers excellent osteoconductivity and bone-implant integration. However, the biological effects of sub-micron topography are unknown. We compared osteoblastic phenotypes and in vivo bone and implant integration abilities between titanium surfaces with micro- (1-5 µm) and sub-micro-scale (0.1-0.5 µm) compartmental structures and machined titanium. The calculated average roughness was 12.5 ± 0.65, 123 ± 6.15, and 24 ± 1.2 nm for machined, micro-rough, and sub-micro-rough surfaces, respectively. In culture studies using bone marrow-derived osteoblasts, the micro-rough surface showed the lowest proliferation and fewest cells attaching during the initial stage. Calcium deposition and expression of osteoblastic genes were highest on the sub-micro-rough surface. The bone-implant integration in the Sprague-Dawley male rat femur model was the strongest on the micro-rough surface. Thus, the biological effects of titanium surfaces are not necessarily proportional to the degree of roughness in osteoblastic cultures or in vivo. Sub-micro-rough titanium ameliorates the disadvantage of micro-rough titanium by restoring cell attachment and proliferation. However, bone integration and the ability to retain cells are compromised due to its lower interfacial mechanical locking. This is the first report on sub-micron topography on a titanium surface promoting osteoblast function with minimal osseointegration.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究钛表面形貌对骨整合的影响，但未涉及增材制造、疲劳或应力屏蔽。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover AM/LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing, fatigue, or stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究亚微米级钛表面形貌对骨整合的生物学效应。
summary_zh.method: 比较加工态、微粗糙和亚微米粗糙钛表面的成骨表型及体内骨整合。
summary_zh.result: 亚微米表面促进细胞附着和增殖，但微粗糙表面骨整合能力更强。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验和SD大鼠股骨模型验证。

summary_en.motivation: The biological effects of sub-micron topography on titanium surfaces for bone-implant integration are not well understood.
summary_en.method: Osteoblastic phenotypes and in vivo bone integration were compared among machined, micro-rough, and sub-micro-rough titanium surfaces.
summary_en.result: Sub-micron topography enhanced cell attachment and osteogenic gene expression but exhibited lower interfacial mechanical locking and in vivo bone integration compared to micro-rough surfaces.
summary_en.validation: In vitro osteoblast cultures and in vivo implantation in Sprague-Dawley rat femurs were used.
